text: EX-99.1 2 ex991gnlearningsrelease930.htm EX-99.1 EARNINGS RELEASE 9.30.26 Document EXHIBIT 99.1 GLOBAL NET LEASE REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS – Closed $535 Million Accretive Modiv Industrial Acquisition and Fully Integrated Acquired Portfolio, Achieving Anticipated G&A Synergies With No Increase in G&A Expense in Third Quarter – Accelerated Reduction in Office Exposure to 23% From 27% at Beginning of Year, With Additional Sales Pending to Further Reduce Exposure to Approximately 18% – Repurchased 6.6 Million Shares for $58.5 Million in Third Quarter 2026 at an AFFO Yield of Approximately 10%, Offering Greater Accretion Than Current STNL Acquisition Opportunities – Maintained Strong Liquidity of $863 Million and Revolving Credit Facility Capacity of $1 Billion; No Debt Maturing Until Fourth Quarter 2027 – Third Quarter 2026 Net Debt to Adjusted EBITDA Temporarily Elevated to 7.7x Due to Timing of Modiv Closing, Reflecting Full Modiv Debt but Only Partial-Quarter Earnings; Reaffirmed Full-Year Net Debt to Adjusted EBITDA Guidance of 6.5x – 6.9x – Reports Q3’26 AFFO Per Share of $0.22; Raises Full-Year AFFO Per Share Guidance to $0.83 – $0.85 New York, November 4, 2026 — Global Net Lease, Inc. (NYSE: GNL) (“GNL” or the “Company”), a publicly traded real estate investment trust that focuses on acquiring and managing a global portfolio of income producing net lease assets across the United States, and Western and Northern Europe, announced today its financial and operating results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Third Quarter 2026 Highlights • Revenue was $112.9 million, compared to $121.0 million in third quarter 2025, primarily reflecting effects of asset dispositions • Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $67.1 million, or $(0.31) per diluted share, compared to $71.1 million, or $(0.32) per diluted share, in third quarter 2025 • Adjusted Funds from Operations (“AFFO”) 1 was $48.3 million, or $0.22 per share, compared to $53.2 million in third quarter 2025, or $0.24 per share, primarily reflecting effects of asset dispositions • Closed the $535 million acquisition of Modiv Industrial on August 12, 2026, and fully integrated its 40-property portfolio, which has a 15.0-year weighted-average remaining lease term and 2.4% average annual rent increases; increasing GNL’s industrial exposure to 51% of portfolio straight-line rent • Closed plus disposition pipeline totaling $391 million 2 , with occupied assets sold at a 7.7% cash cap rate; remaining closed dispositions primarily consist of vacant assets eliminating over $2 million of annualized NOI drag • Continued to execute strategic office reduction strategy with office sales representing 68% of dispositions, reducing office exposure to 23% in third quarter 2026 from 27% of portfolio straight-line rent at the beginning of 2026; further reduction to approximately 18% expected upon completion of pending dispositions • Strategically identified opportunistic sales of car wash and gas and convenience assets, with approximately $70 million under contract at a 6.5% cash cap rate; buyer demand for year-end bonus depreciation benefits supports attractive pricing and an additional source of capital • Continued to deploy net proceeds from non-core asset sales to reduce leverage and strengthen the balance sheet; reduced net debt by $163.8 million since third quarter 2025 • Repurchased 6.6 million shares for a total of $58.5 million in third quarter 2026, bringing total share repurchases under the Share Repurchase Program announced in February 2025 to 29.7 million shares for $245.8 million at a weighted-average price of $8.28 as of October 30, 2026 • Reduced weighted-average interest rate to 4.1% in third quarter 2026, down from 4.2% in third quarter 2025 • Maintained strong liquidity of $863.3 million and Revolving Credit Facility capacity of $1 billion in third quarter 2026, with no debt maturing until the fourth quarter of 2027 GlobalNetLease.com (332) 265-2020 | 650 Fifth Avenue, 30th Floor, New York, NY 10019 • Portfolio occupancy was 96% as of third quarter 2026, with office occupancy increasing to 98% from 94% as of third quarter 2025 • Increased portfolio weighted-average remaining lease term to 6.3 years as of September 30, 2026, up from 5.7 years as of June 30, 2026, reflecting the addition of the Modiv portfolio • Strengthened sector-leading tenant quality with 63% of annualized straight-line rent derived from investment-grade or implied investment-grade tenants 3 , up from 60% in third quarter 2025 • Leased more than 840,000 square feet, achieving a 4.9% renewal leasing spread and a weighted-average renewal term of 5.2 years, resulting in more than $10.4 million of new straight-line rent • Weighted-average annual rent increase of 1.5% provides embedded organic rental growth, excluding approximately 20% of the portfolio with CPI-linked leases that have historically experienced significantly higher rent increases • Reduced annualized G&A expense by over $2.5 million year-over-year, reflecting continued benefits from portfolio simplification and operational efficiencies across a more streamlined operating platform • Reduced recurring capital expenditures to $5.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from $26.2 million in the prior-year period, reflecting a more streamlined portfolio and over $20 million of savings “In the third quarter of 2026, GNL continued to deliver on the priorities we have outlined for shareholders, completing and fully integrating the Modiv Industrial acquisition and accelerating the reduction in our office exposure,” said Michael Weil, Chief Executive Officer of GNL. “The immediately accretive Modiv transaction increased industrial exposure to 51% of portfolio straight-line rent, extended our portfolio weighted-average remaining lease term to 6.3 years and increased our weighted-average annual contractual rent increase to 1.5%, which does not include the approximately 20% of our portfolio with CPI-linked leases. Including those leases, and using historical CPI data, our portfolio’s annual rent growth is approximately 2%. The integration has already delivered the anticipated G&A synergies, and quarterly G&A expense declined from both the prior year and the prior quarter. We reduced GNL’s office exposure to 23% from 27% at the beginning of the year, and we expect to further reduce that exposure to approximately 18% upon completion of pending dispositions. “Our strong liquidity position, investment-grade balance sheet and $391 million of closed plus disposition pipeline, together with no debt maturities until the fourth quarter of 2027, provide the flexibility to advance our strategy without needing to issue common equity or debt in this market. We have strategically identified opportunistic sales of car wash and gas and convenience assets, with approximately $70 million currently under contract at a cash cap rate of 6.5%, supported by buyer demand for year-end bonus depreciation benefits. The expected proceeds provide another source of attractively priced capital, and the ability to monetize assets at these valuations while repurchasing our shares at an AFFO yield of approximately 10% underscores the appeal of this capital allocation strategy. During the quarter, we repurchased 6.6 million shares for $58.5 million, reflecting our view that GNL remains undervalued and that repurchases offered greater accretion than the real estate acquisition opportunities we evaluated. We will remain patient when market conditions do not support accretive acquisitions, while maintaining our focus on reducing office exposure and leverage over time. “Despite market headwinds, we continue to strengthen GNL and see significant opportunities to execute our long-term growth strategy and unlock value for investors. We believe our portfolio’s strong performance and continued progress support raising the low end of our full-year AFFO per share and gross transaction volume guidance ranges, reflecting our confidence in the business and continued focus on creating long-term shareholder value,” Mr. Weil concluded. GlobalNetLease.com (332) 265-2020 | 650 Fifth Avenue, 30th Floor, New York, NY 10019 Caution on Use of Non-GAAP Measures Funds from Operations (“FFO”), Core Funds from Operations (“Core FFO”), Adjusted Funds from Operations (“AFFO”), Adjusted Earnings before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization (“Adjusted EBITDA”), Net Operating Income (“NOI”) and Cash Net Operating Income (“Cash NOI”) and Cash Paid for Interest are non-GAAP financial measures and should not be construed to be more relevant or accurate than the current GAAP methodology in calculating net income or in its applicability in evaluating our operating performance. The method utilized to evaluate the value and performance of real estate under GAAP should be construed as a more relevant measure of operational performance and considered more prominently than the non-GAAP measures. Other REITs may not define FFO in accordance with the current National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts (“NAREIT”) definition (as we do), or may interpret the current NAREIT definition differently than we do, or may calculate Core FFO or AFFO differently than we do. Consequently, our presentation of FFO, Core FFO and AFFO may not be comparable to other similarly-titled measures presented by other REITs in our peer group. We consider FFO, Core FFO and AFFO useful indicators of our performance. Because FFO, Core FFO and AFFO calculations exclude such factors as depreciation and amortization of real estate assets and gains or losses from sales of operating real estate assets (which can vary among owners of identical assets in similar conditions based on historical cost accounting and useful-life estimates), FFO, Core FFO and AFFO presentations facilitate comparisons of operating performance between periods and with other REITs in our peer group. As a result, we believe that the use of FFO, Core FFO and AFFO, together with the required GAAP presentations, provide a more complete understanding of our operating performance including relative to our peers and a more informed and appropriate basis on which to make decisions involving operating, financing, and investing activities. However, FFO, Core FFO and AFFO are not indicative of cash available to fund ongoing cash needs, including the ability to make cash distributions. Investors are cautioned that FFO, Core FFO and AFFO should only be used to assess the sustainability of our operating performance excluding these activities, as they exclude certain costs that have a negative effect on our operating performance during the periods in which these costs are incurred. Funds from Operations, Core Funds from Operations and Adjusted Funds from Operations Funds From Operations Due to certain unique operating characteristics of real estate companies, as discussed below, NAREIT, an industry trade group, has promulgated a measure known as FFO, which we believe to be an appropriate supplemental measure to reflect the operating performance of a REIT. FFO is not equivalent to net income or loss as determined under GAAP. We calculate FFO, a non-GAAP measure, consistent with the standards established over time by the Board of Governors of NAREIT, as restated in a White Paper approved by the Board of Governors of NAREIT effective in December 2018 (the "White Paper"). The White Paper defines FFO as net income or loss computed in accordance with GAAP, excluding depreciation and amortization related to real estate, gain and loss from the sale of certain real estate assets, gain and loss from change in control and impairment write-downs of certain real estate assets and investments in entities when the impairment is directly attributable to decreases in the value of depreciable real estate held by the entity. Adjustments for unconsolidated partnerships and joint ventures are calculated to exclude the proportionate share of the non-controlling interest to arrive at FFO, Core FFO, AFFO and NOI attributable to stockholders, as applicable. Our FFO calculation complies with NAREIT's definition. FFO includes adjustments related to the treatment of the sale of the Multi-Tenant Retail Portfolio as a discontinued operation, which includes adjustments for depreciation and amortization and loss (gain) on dispositions of real estate investments. The historical accounting convention used for real estate assets requires straight-line depreciation of buildings and improvements, and straight-line amortization of intangibles, which implies that the value of a real estate asset diminishes predictably over time.
